valuation.conventions: Peer by PRODUCT overlap, not the 'auto ancillary' label (forging vs wiring-harness is not a comparison). Technology/EV-content names carry a structural premium - quantify it against the content-growth differential rather than accepting or rejecting it. Global peers (Bosch, Aptiv, Schaeffler AG) are context for where multiples can go, never Indian comps.

overlays.business_model: Sector model: volume taker on OEM platforms + content-per-vehicle (CPV) growth + aftermarket annuity. Being spec'd on a platform = 5-7 year revenue visibility; the win happens 12-18 months before revenue. Revenue quality ladder: aftermarket (annuity-like) > platform-backed OEM supply (order-book-backed) > spot/replacement OEM. Tooling income is one-off - separate it from product revenue when judging growth.
overlays.financials: D1: split growth into (a) underlying OEM production growth (SIAM data), (b) CPV/share gains, (c) new-program ramps - a component maker growing at market rate has NO story; 1.5-2x market = content story, verify against production prints. RM pass-through is contractual with a lag (usually quarterly resets): margin compression in commodity-spike quarters recovers 1-2 quarters later - do not call a spike quarter a structural break, and check whether recovery actually arrived. D2: capex-ahead-of-ramp is NORMAL (win -> 12-18m capex -> revenue): CWIP tied to a NAMED program is fine, CWIP without disclosed programs is not. OEM receivables are safe but 60-90 days; aftermarket/export receivables carry real credit risk - split DSO analysis if disclosed. D3: FCF-negative during win-driven capex cycles is acceptable IF program-cycle incremental ROCE clears hurdle - judge the cycle, not the point-in-time FCF.
overlays.supply_chain: Inputs: steel/specialty alloys (forgings), copper (motors/harnesses), rare-earth magnets (e-motors - China export-control single-source risk is live and material), electronics components. Check import dependence per AR forex spend, natural hedge from exports, and pass-through clause coverage. Customer side IS the story: OEM concentration, platform/program mix (growing vs sunset platforms).
overlays.governance: Sector-typical: related-party sales to promoter-owned distributors (aftermarket channel); tooling receivables netted against customer advances; order-book definitions changing between presentations (lifetime-value vs annualized - a silent redefinition is a flag).
overlays.peers: Peer only on product overlap. CPV comparisons across companies use different content definitions - state the definition each company uses or mark non-comparable. Export-heavy vs domestic-heavy names face different demand cycles - note it.
overlays.risks: Sector signatures: EV transition per product line - classify revenue into obsolete-in-BEV (engine internals, fuel systems, exhaust) / agnostic (bearings, seating, lighting, structural) / enhanced (e-motors, e-axles, controllers, sensors, HV harnesses) - the bucket split is THE strategic risk number; customer concentration (one OEM's platform decision can remove a plant's volumes); rare-earth/China dependence; tariff exposure for exporters (US/EU); pass-through lag squeezes in fast commodity spikes; program-ramp execution.
overlays.industry: Derived demand: OEM production prints (SIAM) lead ancillary revenue by ~0-1 quarter. Export names also track US/EU SAAR and OEM announcements. China rare-earth policy news is a sector-wide sensitivity. PLI for advanced components shifts capex economics.
overlays.valuation: The EV-content premium question dominates sector multiples: anchor any premium/discount discussion in the ev_revenue_share taxonomy split and growth_vs_underlying, not in narrative enthusiasm.
overlays.takeaways: Monitorables vocabulary: next SIAM production print, disclosed order-win announcements, program ramp milestones (named plants), rare-earth policy news, quarterly export mix, top-customer platform news.

forensic_signatures: Order-book inflation via changed counting conventions (lifetime vs annual value) - compare definitions across presentations
Tooling income classified as recurring product revenue
CWIP without named programs while 'capacity expansion' is the narrative
Export receivables aging hidden in consolidated DSO
classic_mistakes: Valuing on order-book multiples without conversion history
Missing the pass-through lag - calling a commodity-spike quarter a structural margin break
Crediting EV optionality while ignoring the ICE cash-cow melt rate
Comparing CPV across companies with different content-counting definitions
Treating growth at market rate as a content story
